rationale: Lycopolitan term for cultivator/peasant. Used as the central image for the apostles in this kephalaion: one who selects seed from the beginning, sows in due season, nourishes, and reaps. Synonymous with ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲉ in this passage.
Lycopolitan ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲉ = ⲟⲩⲱⲓⲉ 'farmer, peasant.' Used interchangeably with ⲡⲁⲣⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ in this kephalaion.
Lycopolitan agricultural term for 'seed.' Central to the farming-as-apostolate metaphor.
ϣⲱⲙ = the hot/dry summer season = harvest time. Antithetical pair with ⲡⲣⲱ 'winter.'
The cold/wet season; paired antithetically with ⲡϣⲱⲙ. The two seasons structure the agricultural metaphor: planting/protection (winter) vs. fruiting/harvest (summer).
Lycopolitan ⲱⲉⲥ = ⲱϩⲥ 'to reap, harvest.' The defining act of the harvest season.
Verb of gathering/collecting fruit and seed. Key term in the harvest sequence: reap (ⲱⲉⲥ) → gather (ⲉⲉⲥⲧ) → store (ⲭⲁⲗⲟⲩ ⲉⲙ̄ ⲡϣⲏⲛ).
Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ 'new.' Modifies ⲙⲟⲣⲫⲁⲩⲉ 'form' and ⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ 'church' — the new form/community produced by each apostle.
πλάσμα = 'thing-formed' (Greek loan). Technical Manichaean term for the archonic fashioning of Adam/humanity. The apostolic succession runs ⲭⲛ̄ ⲧⲁⲣⲭⲏ 'from the beginning' of this molding.
ⲥⲁ-ⲛ-ⲧⲡⲉ = 'the side of heaven, the region above.' Spatial cosmological term for the upper heavenly realm where the apostles originate.
ⲙⲁⲉⲉ (Lyc.) = ⲙⲟⲟϣⲉ 'walk' + ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'downward.' The descent of the apostle to the world preserves spatial-soteriological directionality.
Lycopolitan ⲁⲁⲡⲉ = ⲁⲡⲉ 'head' — used in agricultural register for the head of grain or the bound sheaf. The head/sheaf is what the farmer carries and gathers.
